Fit a Conditional Inference Survival Forest

Source: R/fit_cforest.R
fit_cforest.Rd

Fits a survival forest model using the party::cforest() implementation of conditional inference trees for right-censored survival data.

Usage

fit_cforest(
  formula,
  data,
  teststat = "quad",
  testtype = "Univariate",
  mincriterion = 0,
  ntree = 500,
  mtry = 5,
  replace = TRUE,
  fraction = 0.632,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula

A Surv() survival formula specifying the outcome and predictors.

data

A data frame containing the variables in the model.

teststat

Character string specifying the test statistic to use (default = "quad"). See party::cforest_control().

testtype

Character string specifying the type of test (default = "Univariate").

mincriterion

Numeric, the value of the test statistic that must be exceeded for a split to be performed (default = 0).

ntree

Integer, number of trees to grow (default = 500).

mtry

Integer, number of variables randomly selected at each node (default = 5).

replace

Logical, whether sampling of cases is with replacement (default = TRUE).

fraction

Proportion of samples to draw if replace = FALSE (default = 0.632).

...

Additional arguments passed to party::cforest_control().

Value

An object of class "mlsurv_model", containing:

model

The fitted cforest model.

learner

Character string "cforest".

formula

The model formula.

data

The training data.

Details

This function wraps party::cforest() to fit a conditional inference forest for survival analysis, returning an mlsurv_model object compatible with predict_cforest() and the survalis framework.

Examples

mod <- fit_cforest(Surv(time, status) ~ age + celltype + karno, data = veteran)
head(predict_cforest(mod, newdata = veteran[1:5, ], times = c(100, 200)))
#>       t=100     t=200
#> 1 0.5258457 0.2759512
#> 2 0.8285926 0.4212416
#> 3 0.5697253 0.4456722
#> 4 0.5800329 0.3240728
#> 5 0.8203375 0.3783192
